items.title: U.S. Aerospace & Defense: Diving Into Our Supply-Chain Survey
items.summary: Our latest Industry Pulse supplier survey found that commercial aftermarket volume and price growth is strong but decelerating, original-equipment volume and price pressure is building momentum, and many participants flagged mounting supply chain issues/parts shortages as headwinds.

items.title: Gulf Cooperation Council Faces One Shock, Six Trajectories
items.summary: The U.S.-Iran conflict has evolved into a broader macroeconomic shock, with divergent outcomes across the GCC. We assess how the conflict is reshaping the GCC nations' outlook and why its macroeconomic implications differ markedly across the region.

items.title: Quantitative Global Macro Strategy: 'Tis the Season
items.summary: Crowding scores materially shape the market reaction following earnings reports. We explore historical patterns for beats, misses and crowding, and offer a guide to help investors leverage these crowding dynamics to navigate earnings-driven price action.

items.title: U.S. Electrical Equipment: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: We remain constructive on Multis ahead of 3Q earnings. Data center infrastructure investment and improving short-cycle demand should support solid revenue momentum and durable earnings. Risks include price/cost headwinds, higher rates, and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.title: U.S. Machinery: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: Machinery stocks have cooled from summer highs amid macro and policy concerns, but channel feedback suggests demand fundamentals have held up or strengthened. Construction remains our favored sub-sector. We remain more cautious on truck and ag markets than Street expectations.

items.title: U.S. Biotechnology and Pharmaceuticals: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: Biopharma’s backdrop remains constructive heading into 3Q26 EPS, supported by volume growth, rising generalist participation, and receded policy concerns. Commercial fundamentals remain intact, policy risk appears manageable, and several major catalysts are approaching into YE26 and 2027.

items.title: European Banks: Sovereign Fears Seem Misplaced
items.summary: European banks have fallen 6% in October on heightened sovereign concerns. Valuations look undemanding, we see potential for further positive earnings revisions around third-quarter reporting, and believe sovereign fears are misplaced based on sovereign holdings and sensitivity analysis.

items.title: Global Gas and Power Insights: European Gas Balance Eases
items.summary: Europe is injecting gas into storage faster than expected, with storage now over 73% full. In addition to warm weather and weak Asian LNG demand, gas exports from Ukraine and further reductions in European industrial demand have helped improve the gas balance.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Energy Prices Driving Interest Rates
items.summary: Energy price expectations were the main macro driver this week. Fed officials indicated rates could rise further but without urgency. We view the September FOMC minutes as consistent with a pause in October. Cooler inflation should keep the Fed on hold, with cuts penciled in for mid-2027.

items.title: U.S. Rates Weekly: Pension Plan for 20s?
items.summary: We remain neutral on duration despite a strong 10-year auction and expect the FOMC to keep rates unchanged in October. Treasury could signal reductions in long-end auction sizes, with weak pension demand potentially cited as a reason to reduce or cancel the 20-year bond.

items.title: China Economics: Pre-Holiday Mini-Stimulus to Post-Golden Week Fiscal Steps
items.summary: Domestic weakness following Golden Week prompted additional support measures, including recycling unused local government bond quota. Investment-led stabilization remains likely into year-end if construction improves. A 2027 policy pivot appears highly probable, though risks remain.

items.title: India Economics and Strategy: RBI FX Measures
items.summary: RBI announced FX measures that tighten derivative rules and support the rupee by shifting a source of dollar demand. We expect INR appreciation followed by consolidation. The measures raise the cost of rupee depreciation trades but do not remove underlying balance-of-payments pressures.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Will Good Be Good Enough?
items.summary: Q3 earnings revision trends have been solid and tell us that results will be good. We expect a normal beat but with mixed commentary on outlooks. AI-related companies are expected to maintain recent revenue trends, while more macro-sensitive businesses are likely to show conservatism.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Models Race Ahead While Infrastructure Catches Up
items.summary: AI capabilities are advancing, but generating returns requires infrastructure and enterprises to keep pace. Working with communities is key to meeting data center project timelines. The next test will be whether power delivery to data center sites can improve as quickly as the models.

items.title: U.S. Telecom Infrastructure: SpaceX Begins to Assemble Spectrum Layer Cake
items.summary: We view SpaceX's agreement to acquire Grain Management's 800 MHz spectrum portfolio as a net positive for tower stocks, an ongoing risk for Telco and Cable stocks, and a positive for SpaceX's US mobile strategy. We explore the implications and our stock picks herein.

items.title: U.S. Systems Software: Bus Tour Day 3 Takeaways
items.summary: We believe backup, recovery and resilience TAM modernization remains underappreciated. We are most uniformly bullish on PANW and view Vercel's tone and business momentum as a positive read for NET's second-half acceleration prospects. See our detailed session notes herein.

items.title: U.S. Beverages: Takeaways from the 2026 NACS Show
items.summary: The tone at NACS in Las Vegas was more subdued than last year given softer traffic and consumption levels. However, we came away with conviction in continued strong trends for energy drinks, supported by shelf-space gains, new consumer recruitment and product innovation.

items.title: Retail Weekend Reading: It’s Time for an EV Sanity Check
items.summary: We use an Enterprise Value (EV) sanity check to assess relationships between stocks and companies across the retail sector. Reviewing current EVs across our 59 covered companies highlights three relationships that, in our view, do not pass the sanity check and warrant a closer look.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: A French Problem, Not a European One
items.summary: The French problem is a French problem, not a European one. While some contagion is always likely, overall stress may remain focused on France. This could still be enough to avoid the more hawkish ECB path priced. We discuss the implications and related trade ideas herein.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Buying USD
items.summary: We've added to USD longs in our short-term strategy positioning, establishing shorts in CE FX, as we expect further downside in EUR FX and closely linked currencies. We think markets have priced in too much European optimism, and the French OAT spread selloff could begin deflating EUR FX.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: Supply/Demand Trends for OATs
items.summary: OAT supply returns this week and is likely to play a significant role in sustaining OAT cheapness, especially with a heavy net cash need ahead of the presidential election. French banks have been diversifying away from OATs, raising questions about demand absorption.

items.title: UK Economics: Autumn 2026 Budget Preview
items.summary: We expect the Chancellor to deliver a calm and market-positive budget on October 28. We expect he will maintain a minimum headroom buffer between £14–£16 billion in 2029/30, although it is possible he may surprise the market by delivering more. To achieve this buffer, however, we expect him to raise taxes.

items.title: European Brokers & Asset Managers: 3Q26 Preview, EMG Upgrade to Buy
items.summary: European traditional managers’ flows remained healthy in 3Q26, with ex-money market net inflows tracking at more than 4% annualized and broadly stable versus recent quarters. We upgrade EMG to Buy, reflecting improving fundamentals and significant earnings upside potential.

items.title: Visa and MasterCard: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: We expect another healthy quarter from V and MA, supported by resilient consumer spending, improving cross-border trends, and continued strength in value-added services. Given strong outlooks and attractive valuations, we reiterate our Buy ratings on V/MA with target prices of $440/$675.

items.title: Global Battery Chain: A More Balanced Landscape
items.summary: We witnessed the battery price cycle inflection in 2025. Looking ahead as battery capacity catches up, we are not as bearish as the market fears. We see a more balanced supply-demand landscape and expect opportunities to be increasingly value-based and company-specific.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors and Equipment: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: The semiconductor industry remains firmly in Phase 2 of our playbook, supported by robust data center demand and recovery in auto and industrial markets. While the backdrop remains constructive, estimate revision momentum slowed in 2Q and we are becoming increasingly selective.

items.title: U.S. Communications Equipment: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: We remain broadly constructive on networking stocks based on our multi-year AI infrastructure playbook. Our top three Buy-rated picks are ANET, LITE, and KEYS, with rankings influenced by constrained supply — especially silicon and lasers — and impact to the overall gross margins mix.

items.title: U.S. Components, Hardware & Storage: 3Q26 Preview
items.summary: AI demand and capex remain key drivers of robust demand and backlog across our coverage, with visibility supported by long-term contracts. We remain most bullish on connectivity component names as the growth story broadens beyond IT datacom and becomes increasingly content-driven.

items.title: More Oil Flowing out of Mideast, but at High Logistical Cost
items.summary: ICE Brent prices have eased as Middle Eastern oil exports have risen to close to pre-conflict levels. However, higher exports and lower Saudi OSPs are coming alongside very expensive, less efficient logistics, reflected in high freight rates and widening crude oil benchmark differentials.

items.title: Greece: More Rating Upgrades in the Pipeline?
items.summary: Attention is turning to Greece's upcoming rating reviews from S&P and Fitch, where we see scope for further outlook upgrades. However, we do not expect rating upgrades before 2027, with election-year policy commitment remaining an important consideration. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: China Macro Outlook: Approaching Inflection
items.summary: China’s domestic economy is on the verge of recession, but headline growth should still meet 2026's target, with an investment-led cyclical stabilization ahead. The government may be compelled to “protect four” in 2027 amid growth headwinds. We offer further analysis in this presentation.

items.title: Global Theme Machine: Healthcare Momentum Fades
items.summary: September saw a notable reversal in thematic performance, with the top-quintile theme basket lagging MSCI World by 3.6% as investors turned more risk-averse. But relative performance remained intact, with the top quintile outperforming the bottom quintile by 0.8%.

items.title: U.S. Labor-Market Update: September 2026
items.summary: September employment numbers were softer than expected, but the labor market can still broadly be called stable. We'd be cautious about concluding that signals from recent prints indicate a retightening labor market as opposed to one that's shrinking or just growing very slowly.

items.title: U.S. Diversified Utilities: What's the Impact of Higher Rates?
items.summary: We think higher rates could restore relative yield as a more important driver of utility performance after AI/data center growth reduced the traditional focus on income. We look at which names screen least attractive on a historical yield basis and what might happen if rates keep rising.

items.title: Porsche: Setting a (Credible) Dream
items.summary: We've written about the lack of dreams in EU autos, but Porsche has now given us the opposite, confirming all previous recovery targets and setting long-term dream targets. Moreover, it's done so using credible conservative assumptions. This is how you build an investment dream.

items.title: U.S. Aerospace & Defense: Close Enough to a Bottom?
items.summary: We anticipate a volatile third-quarter EPS season for Aerospace & Defense names but think we're close enough to a major bottom in our subsectors that we're again selectively buying dips and expect to follow up with more conviction. We issue positive Catalyst Watches on RTX, VSEC and HII.

items.title: We're Upgrading Kone to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Kone to Buy, with a €63 target price. This Deep Dive into the proposed acquisition of Thyssenkrupp Elevator suggests Kone’s estimate of €700 million in synergies over three years is credible. We also explore antitrust considerations and see a resolution as achievable.

items.title: North America Alternative Energy: Old Reactors, New Tricks
items.summary: The nuclear sector has rebounded following announcements supporting reactor uprates and potential new nuclear investments, reinforcing the growing role of nuclear power in meeting rising electricity demand. We continue to see uprates as the most cost-effective pathway to add generation.

items.title: U.S. Application Software: Bus Tour Takeaways, Day 2
items.summary: We continued our Software bus tour with meetings with Top Picks BOX and NAVN along with INTU and ASAN. Our meetings reinforced the broadening strategic relevance of software as a harness for AI, though the path from product innovation to durable revenue acceleration remains uneven.

items.title: North America Transportation: Earnings Preview
items.summary: Recent declines across Transports have created a more favorable risk-reward setup, even as macro risks seem likely to keep investors cautious. We see the pullback as a healthy correction and think the valuation reset has restored attractive upside. We upgrade XPO to Buy.

items.title: North America Specialty Chemicals: Earnings Preview
items.summary: While we've lowered estimates modestly for industrial gases and specialty chemical companies, we think most can at least deliver maintained guidance given strong pricing ahead of inflation and strong secular growth trends. We see ECL as best positioned into and after the quarter.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Third-Quarter Portfolio Report
items.summary: We offer our quarterly portfolio report. We managed to time our equities exit successfully ahead of the big AI correction and traded a few idiosyncratic themes well, but were wrongly positioned on the Fed and failed to pivot quickly to capture the big USD rally and U.S. front-end selloff.
